Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second innings. Heather Siegers and Phebe Molkenboer to open the innings for the Netherlands Women. Rachel Slater will take the new ball for Scotland Women. Here we go!
…THE RUN CHASE…

Silver Siegers leads the bowling effort for Netherlands Women  -  For the Netherlands Women, as many as nine bowlers were used as they experimented with combinations. Silver Siegers was the standout performer with two wickets, while Iris Zwilling, Myrthe van den Raad, and Isabel van der Woning delivered disciplined spells to maintain pressure throughout the innings. Set a target of 164, the Netherlands Women will need a strong batting performance to begin their campaign on a positive note. Can they chase it down, or will Scotland's bowlers defend a formidable total? Stay tuned for the second innings.

Late surge from Scotland Women helps them post 163/5 -  Useful late contributions from Priyanaz Chatterji and Pippa Sproul propelled Scotland Women to an impressive 163/5 in their 20 overs. After being asked to bat first, Darcey Carter provided a flying start with a brisk 33, although Fraser departed without scoring. Kathryn Bryce and Sarah Bryce then steadied the innings, adding valuable runs through the middle overs and keeping the scoreboard moving at a healthy rate. Scotland lost some momentum shortly after the halfway stage as wickets fell in quick succession. Still, Chatterji and Sproul counterattacked brilliantly in the closing overs to lift the total beyond the 160-run mark.
Just a single to end the innings! Hannah Landheer lands this on a hard length and outside off, Priyanaz Chatterji slices it towards third man for just one. Scotland Women finish on 163/5!

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now! It has been a remarkable turnaround by the groundstaff, who have done exceptionally well to get play underway so quickly after the rain stopped. Even better news is that we are set for a full 20-over contest, bringing the match back to its original length. The players are already out in the middle, clearly eager and raring to go as we finally edge closer to some action. Katherine Fraser and Iris Zwilling are the two Dutch openers. Darcey Carter has the new ball in her hand. Let's play...
Just In! The Netherlands camp has confirmed that Ailsa Lister is unwell and will not be taking part in this match.

The skipper of Scotland Women - Kathryn Bryce says they would have preferred to bat first, but is happy to get out there and set a strong total on the board. She highlights the value of Scotland's preparation, including the tri-series at home and matches against the Netherlands, noting that it has provided a good run-in ahead of the World Cup.

The captain of Netherlands Women - Babette de Leede says that the conditions should assist the seamers early on. She adds that the team’s preparation has been strong, having played a few games in Scotland against Bangladesh and Scotland, and expressed excitement about featuring in their first T20 World Cup.

Netherlands Women - Babette de Leede (C/ WK), Frederique Overdijk, Heather Siegers, Iris Zwilling, Myrthe van den Raad, Phebe Molkenboer, Robine Rijke, Sanya Khurana, Sterre Kalis, Rosalie Lawrence, Caroline de Lange, Hannah Landheer, Silver Siegers, Isabel van der Woning, Lara Leemhuis.

Scotland Women - Megan McColl, Ailsa Lister (WK), Darcey Carter, Priyanaz Chatterji, Katherine Fraser, Kathryn Bryce (C), Pippa Sproul, Sarah Bryce, Chloe Abel, Gabriella Fontenla, Maisie Maceira, Kirstie Gordon, Olivia Bell, Rachel Slater, Abtaha Maqsood.
TOSS - Netherlands Women have won the toss and opted to BOWL first.

UPDATE - 9.25 AM GMT - There is some positive news as the rain has finally stopped and the hover covers are being removed from the square. The two umpires are currently in the middle carrying out an inspection of the pitch and outfield, with a few areas still under observation. However, if the conditions continue to hold and no further rain arrives, there is growing optimism that we could see some cricket.

UPDATE - 9 AM GMT - The visuals don't look promising at the moment, with steady rain still falling in Derby and a few water puddles already forming along the sides of the hover cover. Conditions remain far from ideal, and the groundstaff continue to keep the square well protected. Meanwhile, Andrew Leonard on air has noted that 11.47 AM GMT is the cut-off time for a potential 5-over-a-side contest, so there is still plenty of time left in the window. For now, it's a waiting game, with hopes pinned on the weather easing up to allow at least some action later in the evening.

TOSS DELAYED! According to the Scotland Women’s official Twitter handle, rain has arrived in Derby, with the covers now firmly in place at the County Ground. As a result, the toss has been officially delayed. An updated start time is yet to be confirmed, with conditions being closely monitored.

Underdogs with big ambitions - On the other hand, the Netherlands Women are set to make their maiden appearance at the T20 World Cup. Led by Babette de Leede, the Dutch side boasts several exciting match-winners, including Heather Siegers, Sterre Kalis, and Caroline de Lange. With the ball, Iris Zwilling enters the tournament as the team's leading wicket-taker in the shortest format, while Silver Siegers and Frederique Overdijk will be expected to shoulder much of the bowling responsibility. Though they begin the tournament as underdogs, the Dutch women will be eager to upset a few fancied opponents and make a statement on the global stage. With both teams fine-tuning their preparations ahead of the World Cup, an absorbing contest awaits. Toss and team news are coming up shortly. Stay tuned.

Scotland Women's key pillar - Scotland will once again look to their captain, Kathryn Bryce, whose all-round abilities make her one of the team's most influential players. Support will also be crucial from key contributors such as Katherine Fraser, Sarah Bryce, Abtaha Maqsood, Darcey Carter, Kirstie Gordon, and Priyanaz Chatterji if Scotland are to make a significant impact in the tournament. Playing in familiar conditions, Scotland will be eager to build momentum, make a deep run in the competition, and potentially challenge some of the tournament's more established sides.
... MATCH DAY ...

Final preparations before the real deal - Welcome to our coverage of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup Warm-up Matches 2026. The opening fixture of the day features Netherlands Women taking on Scotland Women at the County Ground in Derby. The two sides recently met in a tri-series, where Scotland emerged victorious in both encounters, underlining their advantage heading into this contest. With the Women's T20 World Cup just around the corner, both teams will use this warm-up match as an opportunity to fine-tune their combinations and assess their preparations ahead of the main event.
